records.source: וַיְהִ֣י׀בִּשְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה בָּֽרְבִיעִי֙ בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֣ה לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ וַאֲנִ֥י בְתֽוֹךְ־הַגּוֹלָ֖ה עַל־נְהַר־כְּבָ֑ר נִפְתְּחוּ֙ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וָאֶרְאֶ֖ה מַרְא֥וֹת אֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And it was in thirty year in the fourth, on [the] fifth of the month, and I [was] among the exiles by [the] river Kebar; were opened the heavens, and I saw visions of God.
pieces: In the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth day, when I was living with the exiles beside the Kebar Canal, the heavens were opened and I saw visions of God.

L.1: And it came about in the thirtieth year, in the fourth [month], on the fifth [day] of the month, as I [was] among the exiles by the river Kebar, [that] the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.

R.1: It was the thirtieth year, on the fifth day of the fourth month. I was living among the exiles by the Kebar Canal. The sky opened, and I saw visions from God.

decisions.choice: the thirtieth year: a date whose starting point is not given
alternatives: the thirtieth year of the exile, when the book was finished
decisions.reason: The book's other dates count the years of King Jehoiachin's exile (verse 2; 8:1; 33:21; 40:1), but this one gives no starting point, and verse 2 adds the usual reckoning beside it. The most common reading takes it as Ezekiel's age: he was a priest (verse 3), and priests began their full service at thirty (Numbers 4:3). Others count from the finding of the book of the law under Josiah in 622 BC (2 Kings 22:8), which also gives 593 BC, or take it as the year the book was finished. The text does not say which.

decisions.choice: the river Kebar: a canal of the Euphrates in Babylonia
decisions.reason: Kebar is not one of the great rivers. Babylonian business records of the fifth century BC name a large canal of this name near the city of Nippur, south of Babylon, which carried water from the Euphrates. The exiles from Judah were settled along it, at Tel-abib (3:15). The word translated "river" is used for canals as well as rivers (Psalm 137:1, "by the rivers of Babylon").

decisions.choice: visions of God: visions that God gave, which show God's glory
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean visions that come from God or visions in which God is seen, and both are true here: the vision is God's gift and shows his glory (verse 28). The same phrase opens the later visions of 8:3 and 40:2.

decisions.choice: And it came about ... I: the book opens with Ezekiel speaking for himself
decisions.reason: The book begins with "And it came about", as many books of narrative do (Joshua 1:1; Ruth 1:1); it is a way of starting an account, not a link to something before it. Ezekiel tells the vision in the first person, and verses 2-3 then step in with a note in the third person.

decisions.choice: the river Kebar (L); the Kebar Canal (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "river", the word the text uses. Balanced and Readable say "canal", which is what the Kebar was (m2), so that readers do not look for it on a map of rivers. Readable says "the sky opened" for "the heavens were opened" (the same word means both) and "visions from God" for the sense in m3.

decisions.choice: in the fourth month, on the fifth day (B); on the fifth day of the fourth month (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives the month and then the day, and leaves "month" and "day" to be understood; Literal brackets them. Balanced keeps the Hebrew order and says "month" and "day"; Readable gives the date in the order English usually uses, and splits the long sentence into short ones.

records.heading: Ezekiel's vision by the Kebar Canal

records.source: בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הִ֚יא הַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַחֲמִישִׁ֔ית לְגָל֖וּת הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ יוֹיָכִֽין׃
records.gloss: On [the] fifth of the month, it [was] the year the fifth of the exile of the king Jehoiachin,
pieces: on the fifth day of the month (this was the fifth year of King Jehoiachin's exile),

L.2: on the fifth of the month, that [was] the fifth year of the exile of King Jehoiachin,

R.2: This was in the fifth year after King Jehoiachin had been taken away as a prisoner.

decisions.choice: the fifth year of the exile of King Jehoiachin: 593 BC
decisions.reason: Jehoiachin, king of Judah, was taken to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar in 597 BC, after a reign of three months, together with the leading people of Jerusalem (2 Kings 24:8-16). Ezekiel was evidently among them. His fifth year of exile was 593 BC, and the fourth month of that year (verse 1) fell in early summer, about July. Ezekiel dates his visions and messages by the years of this exile (8:1; 20:1; 33:21; 40:1), as if the exiled king were still the rightful one.

decisions.choice: it was the fifth year: a note that gives the date by the usual reckoning
decisions.reason: Verses 2-3 speak of Ezekiel in the third person, as a note added to his own words in verse 1. They repeat the day of the month and give the year in the reckoning the rest of the book uses, so that the uncertain "thirtieth year" can be placed. The sentence runs on into verse 3.

decisions.choice: the year in parentheses (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced sets the year in parentheses because it breaks into the sentence, as the Hebrew does. The record ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced, because the sentence goes on into verse 3.

decisions.choice: after King Jehoiachin had been taken away as a prisoner
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the exile of King Jehoiachin": he had been taken away from his land as a prisoner. Readable gives the day once, in verse 1, and makes this a sentence of its own.

records.source: הָיֹ֣ה הָיָ֣ה דְבַר־יְ֠הוָה אֶל־יְחֶזְקֵ֨אל בֶּן־בּוּזִ֧י הַכֹּהֵ֛ן בְּאֶ֥רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֖ים עַל־נְהַר־כְּבָ֑ר וַתְּהִ֥י עָלָ֛יו שָׁ֖ם יַד־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: surely came [the] word of Yahweh to Ezekiel son of Buzi the priest in [the] land of [the] Chaldeans by [the] river Kebar; and was on him there [the] hand of Yahweh.
pieces: the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to the priest Ezekiel son of Buzi, there in the land of the Chaldeans beside the Kebar Canal. There the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came on him.

L.3: the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} surely came to Ezekiel son of Buzi, the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Kebar; and the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was upon him there.

R.3: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word to Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi. Ezekiel was in the land of the Babylonians, by the Kebar Canal. There the power of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came on him.

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD was on him: the LORD's power took hold of him
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power. The phrase is used when the LORD's power seizes a prophet to make him act or to show him a vision (1 Kings 18:46; 2 Kings 3:15). In Ezekiel it comes before each of the great visions (3:14, 22; 8:1; 33:22; 37:1; 40:1), and it marks what follows as the LORD's doing, not the prophet's own.

decisions.choice: surely came: the word came, and came truly
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis, a common Hebrew way of saying that something really happened. The note insists that what Ezekiel saw and heard far from the temple, in a foreign land, was a real word from the LORD.

decisions.choice: Ezekiel the priest: Ezekiel himself was a priest
alternatives: Buzi the priest: his father was the priest
decisions.reason: The word "the priest" can belong to Ezekiel or to his father Buzi, but it is usually taken of Ezekiel, and the book bears it out: he knows the temple and its rules closely (chapters 8; 40-48) and is careful about ritual purity (4:14). He belonged to the priestly families taken to Babylon with Jehoiachin. His name means "God strengthens" or "may God make strong", and God's promise to make him hard and strong against the people (3:8-9) seems to play on it.

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD was upon him (L); came on him (B); the power of the LORD came on him (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula in Ezekiel: Literal says "was upon", Balanced "came on", and Readable says what the hand stands for (m1), as 2 Kings 3:15 does. Ezekiel's later accounts use the same words in the first person ("upon me", "on me").

decisions.choice: spoke his word (R); the Babylonians (R)
decisions.reason: Readable makes the LORD the subject of the sentence ("spoke his word to"), which says the same as "the word of the LORD came to" in plainer English. It says "Babylonians" for "Chaldeans", as in Isaiah and Jeremiah, and names Ezekiel again so that the long sentence can be split.

records.source: וָאֵ֡רֶא וְהִנֵּה֩ ר֨וּחַ סְעָרָ֜ה בָּאָ֣ה מִן־הַצָּפ֗וֹן עָנָ֤ן גָּדוֹל֙ וְאֵ֣שׁ מִתְלַקַּ֔חַת וְנֹ֥גַֽהּ ל֖וֹ סָבִ֑יב וּמִ֨תּוֹכָ֔הּ כְּעֵ֥ין הַחַשְׁמַ֖ל מִתּ֥וֹךְ הָאֵֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: And I looked, and see, a wind of storm coming from the north, a cloud great and fire taking hold of itself, and brightness to it all around, and from its midst like [the] appearance of the chashmal, from [the] midst of the fire.
pieces: As I looked, I saw a storm wind coming from the north: a huge cloud with fire flashing through it and brightness all around it. In the middle of the fire was something that looked like gleaming metal.

L.4: And I looked, and see, a stormy wind was coming from the north, a great cloud, and fire flashing back and forth, and brightness [was] all around it, and from its midst [there was something] like the appearance of amber, from the midst of the fire.

R.4: I looked and saw a windstorm coming from the north. There was a huge cloud with fire flashing in it, and a bright light shone all around it. In the middle of the fire was something that looked like shining metal.

decisions.choice: chashmal: a substance that shines brightly in fire; what it is, is uncertain
alternatives: electrum (an alloy of gold and silver)
decisions.reason: The word occurs only in Ezekiel (here, verse 27 and 8:2), and its meaning is not known. The setting shows that it gleams with a bright, fiery light. The Greek translation renders it with a word for electrum, an alloy of gold and silver, which was also the word for amber; later tradition followed it. Since the word cannot be pinned down, each rendering gives a general sense of brilliance.

decisions.choice: fire taking hold of itself: fire flashing back and forth without stopping
decisions.reason: The same unusual form is used of the fire that ran through the hail in Egypt (Exodus 9:24). It pictures flames, or lightning, catching and leaping again and again inside the cloud. Storm, cloud and fire are the signs of the LORD's coming in other places too (Exodus 19:16-18; Psalm 18:8-16).

decisions.choice: from the north: the direction from which judgment would come on Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Storms came from the north (Job 37:22), and so did the armies that invaded Israel. Jeremiah had seen disaster coming "from the north" on Jerusalem (Jeremiah 1:13-15). Here the LORD himself comes from that direction to meet the exiles in Babylon.

decisions.choice: amber (L); gleaming metal (B); shining metal (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for *chashmal* in Ezekiel (1:4, 27; 8:2). Literal keeps the old rendering "amber", which goes back to the Greek. Balanced and Readable say "gleaming metal" and "shining metal", which give the brilliance the setting requires without claiming to know the substance (m1). A footnote gives the uncertainty.

decisions.choice: see (L); I saw (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word that points to something seen, traditionally "behold", is "see" at Literal. Balanced and Readable fold it into "I looked and saw". Balanced and Readable use "something that looked like" for "like the appearance of", the hedge set for this chapter (see 1:28).

records.source: וּמִ֨תּוֹכָ֔הּ דְּמ֖וּת אַרְבַּ֣ע חַיּ֑וֹת וְזֶה֙ מַרְאֵֽיהֶ֔ן דְּמ֥וּת אָדָ֖ם לָהֵֽנָּה׃
records.gloss: And from its midst [the] likeness of four living creatures, and this [was] their appearance: [the] likeness of a human [was] to them.
pieces: Out of the middle of it came something that looked like four living creatures. This is what they looked like: they had the form of {{gender:a human being|a man}}.

L.5: And from its midst [came] the likeness of four living creatures, and this [was] how they appeared: they had {{gender:a human|a man's}} likeness.

R.5: Out of the middle of the fire came what looked like four living creatures. They were shaped like {{gender:human beings|men}},

decisions.choice: living creatures: living beings, not yet named
decisions.reason: The word means simply living things, animals or creatures. Ezekiel does not name them here. When he sees them again in chapter 10 he recognizes them as cherubim (10:15, 20), the winged guardians of God's throne pictured over the ark of the covenant (Exodus 25:18-22).

decisions.choice: likeness: the first of the vision's hedges
decisions.reason: The word means a likeness or resemblance, something seen that is like something else. Ezekiel uses it, with "appearance", again and again through the chapter: he describes what he saw by comparing it with things he knew, and never claims that it simply was those things. See the note at 1:28.

decisions.choice: a human: a human being, not a man in particular
decisions.reason: The word is the one for a human being or humankind. It says that the creatures had a human shape, standing upright, before the faces and wings of verses 6-11 are described.

decisions.choice: something that looked like (B); what looked like (R)
decisions.reason: The table for Ezekiel keeps "the likeness of" at Literal and says "something that looked like" at Balanced and Readable, which keeps the hedge in plain words (see 1:28). Readable says "out of the middle of the fire" for "from its midst", from verse 4, and lets the sentence run on into verse 6.

decisions.choice: a human / a man (gender setting)
decisions.reason: The word means a human being, so the inclusive wording is the default and "a man", the traditional rendering, is the alternative, as in Revelation 4:7.

records.source: וְאַרְבָּעָ֥ה פָנִ֖ים לְאֶחָ֑ת וְאַרְבַּ֥ע כְּנָפַ֖יִם לְאַחַ֥ת לָהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And four faces to [each] one, and four wings to [each] one of them.
pieces: Each of them had four faces and four wings.

L.6: And four faces [were] to each one, and four wings to each one of them.

R.6: but each one had four faces and four wings.

decisions.choice: four faces and four wings: a creature unlike any on earth
decisions.reason: Winged creatures with the bodies of several animals guarded thrones and temples in the art of the ancient Near East; the great winged bulls with human heads at the gates of Assyrian palaces are well known. Ezekiel's creatures go beyond anything in that art: each has four faces looking out in four directions (verse 10), so that it never has to turn (verse 9).

decisions.choice: but (R)
decisions.reason: Readable joins the verse to verse 5 with "but", because it has just said that the creatures were shaped like human beings, and the faces and wings are what made them different.

records.source: וְרַגְלֵיהֶ֖ם רֶ֣גֶל יְשָׁרָ֑ה וְכַ֣ף רַגְלֵיהֶ֗ם כְּכַף֙ רֶ֣גֶל עֵ֔גֶל וְנֹ֣צְצִ֔ים כְּעֵ֖ין נְחֹ֥שֶׁת קָלָֽל׃
records.gloss: And their feet [were] a foot straight, and [the] sole of their feet like [the] sole of [the] foot of a calf, and sparkling like [the] appearance of bronze burnished.
pieces: Their legs were straight, and their feet were like a calf's hooves. They sparkled like polished bronze.

L.7: And their legs [were] straight legs, and the soles of their feet [were] like the sole of a calf's foot, and they were sparkling like the appearance of polished bronze.

R.7: Their legs were straight. Their feet were like a calf's hooves, and they shone like polished bronze.

decisions.choice: their legs were straight legs: the legs were straight and did not bend
decisions.reason: The same word means foot and leg. The first use here must be the whole leg, since it is called straight; the sole of the foot follows. Straight legs, perhaps with no bending joint, fit creatures that never turned as they moved (verses 9, 12) but went straight ahead.

decisions.choice: polished bronze: bronze burnished until it gleams
decisions.reason: The last word occurs only here and in Daniel 10:6, where the man in linen has arms and legs "like the gleam of burnished bronze". Revelation 1:15 takes up the picture.

decisions.choice: a calf's hooves (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the sole of a calf's foot". Balanced and Readable say "hooves", which is what a calf's foot is, and Readable says "shone" for "sparkled".

records.source: וִידֵ֣י אָדָ֗ם מִתַּ֨חַת֙ כַּנְפֵיהֶ֔ם עַ֖ל אַרְבַּ֣עַת רִבְעֵיהֶ֑ם וּפְנֵיהֶ֥ם וְכַנְפֵיהֶ֖ם לְאַרְבַּעְתָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And hands of a human [were] under their wings on their four sides, and their faces and their wings [belonged] to the four of them.
pieces: Under their wings on their four sides they had {{gender:human hands|the hands of a man}}. As for the faces and wings of the four of them,

L.8: And hands of {{gender:a human|a man}} [were] under their wings on their four sides, and the four of them [had] their faces and their wings [thus]:

R.8: Under their wings, on all four sides, they had {{gender:human hands|hands like a man's}}. All four creatures had faces and wings.

decisions.choice: and hands: the reading tradition, against the written "and his hands"
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the Hebrew text read "and his hands", but the scribes' marginal note tells the reader to say "and hands of", which fits the phrase "hands of a human". The reading in the margin is followed. The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: the four of them had their faces and their wings: a heading for what follows
decisions.reason: The last clause names the faces and wings again, and verses 9-11 describe them: first the wings (verse 9), then the faces (verse 10), then the wings again (verse 11). It is best read as introducing that description.

decisions.choice: human hands / hands of a man (gender setting)
decisions.reason: As in verse 5, the word means a human being, so the inclusive wording is the default. Balanced lets the sentence run on into verse 9, as the Hebrew does; Readable makes the last clause a sentence of its own.

records.source: חֹֽבְרֹ֛ת אִשָּׁ֥ה אֶל־אֲחוֹתָ֖הּ כַּנְפֵיהֶ֑ם לֹא־יִסַּ֣בּוּ בְלֶכְתָּ֔ן אִ֛ישׁ אֶל־עֵ֥בֶר פָּנָ֖יו יֵלֵֽכוּ׃
records.gloss: [were] joined a woman to her sister their wings; not they turned when they went; each in the direction of his face they went.
pieces: their wings touched one another. As they moved they did not turn; each of them went straight ahead.

L.9: Their wings [were] touching each one its sister; they did not turn when they went; each went in the direction of its face.

R.9: Each creature's wings touched the wings of the creature next to it. When they moved, they did not turn around. Each one went straight forward.

decisions.choice: a woman to her sister: one another
decisions.reason: Hebrew uses "a man ... his brother" for "one another", and "a woman ... her sister" when the nouns are feminine, as "wings" is here. Nothing about women is meant. The wings of each creature touched those of the creatures beside it, so that the four formed one square.

decisions.choice: each went in the direction of its face: they could go any way without turning
decisions.reason: Each creature had a face toward each of the four directions (verse 10). Whichever way they went, a face was looking that way, so they moved straight ahead without turning (verses 12, 17).

decisions.choice: each one its sister (L); one another (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the idiom; Balanced and Readable say what it means (m1). Readable spells out whose wings touched whose.

records.source: וּדְמ֣וּת פְּנֵיהֶם֮ פְּנֵ֣י אָדָם֒ וּפְנֵ֨י אַרְיֵ֤ה אֶל־הַיָּמִין֙ לְאַרְבַּעְתָּ֔ם וּפְנֵי־שׁ֥וֹר מֵֽהַשְּׂמֹ֖אול לְאַרְבַּעְתָּ֑ן וּפְנֵי־נֶ֖שֶׁר לְאַרְבַּעְתָּֽן׃
records.gloss: And [the] likeness of their faces: [the] face of a human, and [the] face of a lion to the right [belonged] to the four of them, and [the] face of an ox from the left [belonged] to the four of them, and [the] face of an eagle [belonged] to the four of them.
pieces: This is what their faces looked like: each of the four had {{gender:a human face|the face of a man}}, the face of a lion on the right, the face of an ox on the left, and the face of an eagle.

L.10: And the likeness of their faces: [each had] the face of {{gender:a human|a man}}, and the face of a lion [was] on the right for the four of them, and the face of an ox on the left for the four of them, and the face of an eagle for the four of them.

R.10: This is what their faces looked like. Each of the four had {{gender:a human face|a man's face}} in front. It had a lion's face on the right side and an ox's face on the left side. It also had an eagle's face.

decisions.choice: the four faces: the living creatures of Revelation 4
decisions.reason: Revelation 4:6-8 takes up this vision: around God's throne are four living creatures, full of eyes, the first like a lion, the second like an ox, the third with a human face and the fourth like a flying eagle. There each creature has one of the faces and six wings, as the seraphim of Isaiah 6:2 have. The four faces are often read as the noblest of living things: human beings, the wild animals (the lion), the tame animals (the ox) and the birds (the eagle). From the second century, Christian writers such as Irenaeus linked them with the four Gospels; that is a later reading of the picture.

decisions.choice: the human face in front, the eagle behind
decisions.reason: Only the lion and the ox are given a side, right and left. The human face, named first, is best taken as the face looking forward, and the eagle as the face looking back.

decisions.choice: in front (R); It also had (R)
decisions.reason: Readable adds "in front" for the human face, which the sides given for the lion and the ox imply (m2); it does not say where the eagle's face was, as the text does not. Balanced and Readable give the faces once for all four, where the Hebrew repeats "the four of them" after each one.

decisions.choice: a human face / the face of a man (gender setting)
decisions.reason: As in verse 5, the inclusive wording is the default, as in Revelation 4:7.

records.source: וּפְנֵיהֶ֕ם וְכַנְפֵיהֶ֥ם פְּרֻד֖וֹת מִלְמָ֑עְלָה לְאִ֗ישׁ שְׁ֚תַּיִם חֹבְר֣וֹת אִ֔ישׁ וּשְׁתַּ֣יִם מְכַסּ֔וֹת אֵ֖ת גְּוִיֹתֵיהֶֽנָה׃
records.gloss: And their faces. And their wings [were] spread out from above; to each two [were] joining each, and two [were] covering their bodies.
pieces: Such were their faces. Their wings were spread out above them. Each had two wings that touched the wings of the creature on either side, and two that covered its body.

L.11: And [such were] their faces. And their wings were spread out above; each had two [wings] touching [those of] the other, and two covering their bodies.

R.11: That is what their faces were like. Their wings were spread out above them. Each creature had two wings that touched the wings of the creatures next to it. It had two other wings that covered its body.

decisions.choice: and their faces: the end of the description of the faces
alternatives: their faces and their wings were spread out above
decisions.reason: The verse opens with two words, "and their faces", that do not make a clause of their own. They are best read as closing verse 10: "such were their faces". Some join them to the next words, "their faces and their wings were spread out above", but faces are not spread out. The words may also have been repeated from verse 8 by a copyist.

decisions.choice: two covering their bodies: reverence before God
decisions.reason: The seraphim of Isaiah 6:2 cover their faces and their feet with their wings in the LORD's presence. The creatures here cover their bodies, a sign of reverence and modesty before the one enthroned above them (verse 26).

decisions.choice: the wings of the creature on either side (B); the creatures next to it (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says that two wings were "joining each". Balanced and Readable say whose wings they joined, from verse 9.

records.source: וְאִ֛ישׁ אֶל־עֵ֥בֶר פָּנָ֖יו יֵלֵ֑כוּ אֶ֣ל אֲשֶׁר֩ יִֽהְיֶה־שָׁ֨מָּה הָר֤וּחַ לָלֶ֨כֶת֙ יֵלֵ֔כוּ לֹ֥א יִסַּ֖בּוּ בְּלֶכְתָּֽן׃
records.gloss: And each toward [the] direction of his face they went; to where it was there the spirit to go they went; not they turned when they went.
pieces: Each one went straight ahead. Wherever the spirit would go, they went, and they did not turn as they moved.

L.12: And each went in the direction of its face; wherever the spirit was to go, they went; they did not turn when they went.

R.12: Each one moved straight ahead. They went wherever the spirit wanted to go, and they did not turn as they moved.

decisions.choice: the spirit: the power that moved the creatures; whose spirit it is the text leaves open
decisions.reason: The word means wind, breath or spirit. Here it is what decides where the creatures go, so it is more than wind, though the vision began with a storm wind (verse 4). Verse 20 calls it "the spirit of the living creature", the life that drives both the creatures and the wheels. It may be the LORD's own Spirit moving them, as the Spirit lifts and carries Ezekiel (2:2; 3:12, 14), but the chapter does not say so, and the word is kept lowercase.

decisions.choice: the spirit, lowercase (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Ezekiel's rule for this word gives the sense the setting requires and capitalizes "Spirit" only for God's Spirit. Since the text does not say whose spirit this is (m1), every level has "spirit" in lowercase, and a footnote gives the other readings. Readable says "wanted to go" for "was to go".

records.source: וּדְמ֨וּת הַחַיּ֜וֹת מַרְאֵיהֶ֣ם כְּגַחֲלֵי־אֵ֗שׁ בֹּֽעֲרוֹת֙ כְּמַרְאֵ֣ה הַלַּפִּדִ֔ים הִ֕יא מִתְהַלֶּ֖כֶת בֵּ֣ין הַחַיּ֑וֹת וְנֹ֣גַהּ לָאֵ֔שׁ וּמִן־הָאֵ֖שׁ יוֹצֵ֥א בָרָֽק׃
records.gloss: And [the] likeness of the living creatures: their appearance like coals of fire burning, like [the] appearance of the torches; it [was] going about between the living creatures, and brightness to the fire, and from the fire going out lightning.
pieces: As for the appearance of the living creatures, they looked like burning coals of fire or like torches. Fire moved back and forth among the creatures. It was bright, and lightning flashed out of it.

L.13: And the likeness of the living creatures: their appearance [was] like coals of fire, burning, like the appearance of torches; it was moving to and fro among the living creatures, and the fire [had] brightness, and out of the fire lightning was going out.

R.13: The living creatures looked like burning coals or like torches. Fire kept moving back and forth among them. The fire was very bright, and lightning flashed out of it.

decisions.choice: it was moving to and fro: the fire moved among the creatures
decisions.reason: The word "it" is feminine, as "fire" is, and the end of the verse speaks of "the fire", so it is the fire that moves among the creatures. The verb pictures it going back and forth without rest, like the fire of verse 4.

decisions.choice: burning coals of fire: the coals of 10:2
decisions.reason: In chapter 10 a man in linen is told to take coals of fire from between the cherubim and scatter them over Jerusalem (10:2, 6-7). The fire of the vision is holy fire, as the coal from the altar in Isaiah 6:6, and it can bring judgment.

decisions.choice: As for the appearance (B); looked like (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "looked like" for "their appearance was like". The hedge is kept in plain words (see 1:28). Readable leaves out "of fire" after "coals", which "burning" already says.

records.source: וְהַחַיּ֖וֹת רָצ֣וֹא וָשׁ֑וֹב כְּמַרְאֵ֖ה הַבָּזָֽק׃
records.gloss: And the living creatures [were] running and returning like [the] appearance of the flash.
pieces: The living creatures darted back and forth like flashes of lightning.

L.14: And the living creatures were running and returning like the appearance of a flash of lightning.

R.14: The living creatures darted back and forth like flashes of lightning.

decisions.choice: a flash: a flash of lightning
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here. It is probably a form related to the word for lightning at the end of verse 13, and the comparison is with the speed and brightness of lightning as the creatures dart to and fro.

decisions.choice: running and returning (L); darted back and forth (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the two verbs. Balanced and Readable say "darted back and forth", a single English picture of the same quick movement.

records.source: וָאֵ֖רֶא הַחַיּ֑וֹת וְהִנֵּה֩ אוֹפַ֨ן אֶחָ֥ד בָּאָ֛רֶץ אֵ֥צֶל הַחַיּ֖וֹת לְאַרְבַּ֥עַת פָּנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And I saw the living creatures, and see, a wheel one [was] on the ground beside the living creatures, for its four faces.
pieces: As I watched the living creatures, I saw a wheel on the ground next to each of the four creatures.

L.15: And I looked at the living creatures, and see, [there was] one wheel on the ground beside the living creatures, for each of its four faces.

R.15: As I watched the living creatures, I saw a wheel on the ground next to each one.

decisions.choice: one wheel ... for its four faces: one wheel beside each of the four creatures
alternatives: a single wheel facing four ways
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is brief: "one wheel on the ground beside the living creatures, for its four faces". It is best read as one wheel for each of the four creatures, since verse 16 speaks of "the four of them" and verse 19 of the wheels beside the creatures. Some read it as one wheel that faced in four directions.

decisions.choice: a wheel: the throne moves like a chariot
decisions.reason: With wheels beneath it, the throne of verse 26 is pictured as a chariot that can go anywhere, even to Babylon. 1 Chronicles 28:18 speaks of "the chariot" of the cherubim over the ark, and later Jewish tradition called this vision "the chariot". The LORD is not bound to the temple in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: beside each of the four creatures (B); beside each of them (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the reading taken in m1. Literal keeps "for each of its four faces", with "each of" in brackets.

records.source: מַרְאֵ֨ה הָאוֹפַנִּ֤ים וּמַעֲשֵׂיהֶם֙ כְּעֵ֣ין תַּרְשִׁ֔ישׁ וּדְמ֥וּת אֶחָ֖ד לְאַרְבַּעְתָּ֑ן וּמַרְאֵיהֶם֙ וּמַ֣עֲשֵׂיהֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יִהְיֶ֥ה הָאוֹפַ֖ן בְּת֥וֹךְ הָאוֹפָֽן׃
records.gloss: [The] appearance of the wheels and their work like [the] gleam of tarshish, and likeness one to the four of them, and their appearance and their work as when it is the wheel in [the] midst of the wheel.
pieces: The wheels and the way they were made looked like the sparkle of chrysolite. All four looked alike, and they seemed to be made like a wheel within a wheel.

L.16: The appearance of the wheels and their construction [was] like the gleam of chrysolite, and the four of them [had] one likeness; and their appearance and their construction [were] as if a wheel [were] in the middle of a wheel.

R.16: The wheels sparkled like a gem called chrysolite. All four wheels looked the same. Each seemed to be made like a wheel inside another wheel.

decisions.choice: tarshish: a precious stone, perhaps chrysolite
decisions.reason: The stone is named after Tarshish, a distant land of trade. It is one of the stones of the high priest's breastpiece (Exodus 28:20), and its identity is uncertain: chrysolite, beryl, topaz and yellow jasper have all been proposed. Daniel's heavenly man has a body like it (Daniel 10:6). The wording follows Exodus 28:20.

decisions.choice: a wheel in the middle of a wheel: two wheels set crosswise
alternatives: one wheel inside another, with the same center
decisions.reason: Ezekiel does not explain how the wheels were made. The next verse says that they could go in any of four directions without turning, which suggests two wheels set through each other at right angles. Others picture one wheel inside another, with the same center.

decisions.choice: a gem called chrysolite (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says that chrysolite is a gem, since few readers know the name. Balanced says "the way they were made" for "their construction".

records.source: עַל־אַרְבַּ֥עַת רִבְעֵיהֶ֖ן בְּלֶכְתָּ֣ם יֵלֵ֑כוּ לֹ֥א יִסַּ֖בּוּ בְּלֶכְתָּֽן׃
records.gloss: On their four sides in their going they went; not they turned when they went.
pieces: When they moved, they could go in any of the four directions without turning as they went.

L.17: When they went, they went toward [any of] their four sides; they did not turn when they went.

R.17: They could move in any of the four directions. They did not have to turn when they moved.

decisions.choice: on their four sides: in any of the four directions
decisions.reason: The wheels, like the creatures (verse 9), faced all four ways at once, so they could roll in any direction without turning. The repeated "they did not turn when they went" links the wheels with the creatures (verses 9, 12).

decisions.choice: could go in any of the four directions (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "any of the four directions", the sense of "on their four sides" (m1). Literal brackets "any of".

records.source: וְגַ֨בֵּיהֶ֔ן וְגֹ֥בַהּ לָהֶ֖ם וְיִרְאָ֣ה לָהֶ֑ם וְגַבֹּתָ֗ם מְלֵאֹ֥ת עֵינַ֛יִם סָבִ֖יב לְאַרְבַּעְתָּֽן׃
records.gloss: And their rims, and height to them, and fear to them; and their rims [were] full of eyes all around [to] the four of them.
pieces: Their rims were high and awe-inspiring, and the rims of all four were full of eyes all around.

L.18: And their rims, they [had] height, and they [had] awesomeness; and their rims [were] full of eyes all around, the four of them.

R.18: The rims of the wheels were tall and frightening to see. The rims of all four wheels were covered with eyes all the way around.

decisions.choice: awesomeness: the rims inspired fear
decisions.reason: The word means fear or awe: the rims were frightening to look at. The consonants of this word are close to those of "and I saw", and the Greek translation reads "and I saw them"; but the Hebrew makes sense as it stands.

decisions.choice: full of eyes: seeing everything
decisions.reason: Eyes stand for watchfulness and knowledge. Zechariah 4:10 speaks of "the eyes of the LORD, which range through all the earth", and the living creatures of Revelation 4:6, 8 are "full of eyes". In 10:12 the cherubim themselves, as well as the wheels, are full of eyes.

decisions.choice: high and awe-inspiring (B); tall and frightening to see (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the two nouns. Balanced and Readable turn them into describing words. Readable says the rims were "covered with" eyes, which is what "full of eyes" means here.

records.source: וּבְלֶ֨כֶת֙ הַֽחַיּ֔וֹת יֵלְכ֥וּ הָאוֹפַנִּ֖ים אֶצְלָ֑ם וּבְהִנָּשֵׂ֤א הַֽחַיּוֹת֙ מֵעַ֣ל הָאָ֔רֶץ יִנָּשְׂא֖וּ הָאוֹפַנִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And in [the] going of the living creatures went the wheels beside them, and in [the] being lifted of the living creatures from on the ground were lifted the wheels.
pieces: Whenever the living creatures moved, the wheels went along beside them, and whenever the creatures rose off the ground, the wheels rose as well.

L.19: And as the living creatures went, the wheels went beside them, and as the living creatures were lifted up from the ground, the wheels were lifted up.

R.19: When the living creatures moved, the wheels moved with them. When the creatures rose from the ground, the wheels rose too.

decisions.choice: the wheels went ... the wheels were lifted up: the wheels move with the creatures
decisions.reason: The wheels do not move by themselves: they go, rise and stop with the creatures (verse 21). Verse 20 gives the reason: the creatures' spirit was in them.

decisions.choice: rose (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "were lifted up", the passive the Hebrew uses. Balanced and Readable say "rose", since nothing is said about who lifted them.

records.source: עַ֣ל אֲשֶׁר֩ יִֽהְיֶה־שָּׁ֨ם הָר֤וּחַ לָלֶ֨כֶת֙ יֵלֵ֔כוּ שָׁ֥מָּה הָר֖וּחַ לָלֶ֑כֶת וְהָאוֹפַנִּ֗ים יִנָּשְׂאוּ֙ לְעֻמָּתָ֔ם כִּ֛י ר֥וּחַ הַחַיָּ֖ה בָּאוֹפַנִּֽים׃
records.gloss: To where it was there the spirit to go they went, there the spirit to go, and the wheels were lifted close to them, for [the] spirit of the living creature [was] in the wheels.
pieces: Wherever the spirit would go, they went, and the wheels rose along with them, for the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.

L.20: Wherever the spirit was to go, they went, there [where] the spirit [was] to go; and the wheels were lifted up alongside them, because the spirit of the living creature [was] in the wheels.

R.20: Wherever the spirit wanted to go, the creatures went, and the wheels rose with them. This was because the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.

decisions.choice: there the spirit was to go: a repetition
decisions.reason: The words "there the spirit was to go" repeat the line before them. The repetition may stress that the creatures went exactly where the spirit went, or the words may have been copied twice by a scribe. The sense is the same either way.

decisions.choice: the spirit of the living creature: the life that moved them all
decisions.reason: "The living creature" is singular here and in verses 21-22, though four creatures are meant: the four with their wheels move as one. The spirit is the same as in verse 12; see the note there. The wheels had no life of their own; the creatures' spirit was in them.

decisions.choice: the living creatures, plural (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the singular "the living creature". Balanced and Readable say "creatures", since the four are meant (m2). Readable names "the creatures" for "they".

records.source: בְּלֶכְתָּ֣ם יֵלֵ֔כוּ וּבְעָמְדָ֖ם יַֽעֲמֹ֑דוּ וּֽבְהִנָּשְׂאָ֞ם מֵעַ֣ל הָאָ֗רֶץ יִנָּשְׂא֤וּ הָאֽוֹפַנִּים֙ לְעֻמָּתָ֔ם כִּ֛י ר֥וּחַ הַחַיָּ֖ה בָּאוֹפַנִּֽים׃
records.gloss: In their going they went, and in their standing they stood, and in their being lifted from on the ground were lifted the wheels close to them, for [the] spirit of the living creature [was] in the wheels.
pieces: When the creatures went, the wheels went; when the creatures halted, the wheels halted; and when the creatures rose from the ground, the wheels rose with them, for the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.

L.21: When they went, these went; and when they stood still, these stood still; and when they were lifted up from the ground, the wheels were lifted up alongside them, because the spirit of the living creature [was] in the wheels.

R.21: When the creatures moved, the wheels moved. When the creatures stopped, the wheels stopped. When the creatures rose from the ground, the wheels rose with them. This was because the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.

decisions.choice: they ... these: the creatures and the wheels
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has only verbs: "when they went, they went". The first "they" is the creatures and the second the wheels, as the end of the verse makes clear. The verse sums up verses 19-20.

decisions.choice: the creatures ... the wheels (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the creatures and the wheels so that the reader can tell the two apart (m1). Literal says "these" for the second "they", and "the living creature" stays singular there, as in verse 20.

records.source: וּדְמ֞וּת עַל־רָאשֵׁ֤י הַחַיָּה֙ רָקִ֔יעַ כְּעֵ֖ין הַקֶּ֣רַח הַנּוֹרָ֑א נָט֥וּי עַל־רָאשֵׁיהֶ֖ם מִלְמָֽעְלָה׃
records.gloss: And a likeness over [the] heads of the living creature: a vault, like [the] gleam of the ice the awesome, spread out over their heads from above.
pieces: Over the heads of the living creatures was something like a vault, glittering like ice and awe-inspiring to see, spread out above their heads.

L.22: And [there was] a likeness over the heads of the living creature, a vault, like the gleam of awe-inspiring ice, spread out over their heads above.

R.22: Above the heads of the living creatures was something that looked like a dome. It sparkled like ice, and it was frightening to see. It was spread out over their heads.

decisions.choice: a vault: a solid-looking expanse, the platform beneath the throne
decisions.reason: The word is the one used in Genesis 1:6-8 for the vault of the sky, a solid-looking expanse like a sheet of beaten metal. Here it is spread out over the creatures' heads, and the throne stands on it (verse 26). It is the floor of the heavenly throne room, seen from below, and it holds the LORD's throne above the world, as the sky does.

decisions.choice: awe-inspiring ice: a dazzling, clear surface
decisions.reason: The word means ice or frost (Job 38:29), here ice so bright that it fills the viewer with awe. Some take it as rock crystal, which the ancients thought of as ice that had hardened. The picture is of something clear and brilliant. Exodus 24:10 describes the floor under the God of Israel as "like the very heavens for clearness", and Revelation 4:6 sees before the throne "a sea of glass, like crystal".

decisions.choice: vault (L, B); dome (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this word in Ezekiel 1:22-26, as in Genesis 1:6: "vault", an arched ceiling that is solid, at Literal and Balanced, and "dome" at Readable (m1). "Firmament", the old word, is little known now, and "expanse" loses the sense of something solid.

decisions.choice: something like (B); something that looked like (R); the living creatures, plural (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the hedge "likeness" in plain words (see 1:28). Balanced and Readable say "creatures" for the collective singular, as in verse 20.

records.source: וְתַ֨חַת֙ הָרָקִ֔יעַ כַּנְפֵיהֶ֣ם יְשָׁר֔וֹת אִשָּׁ֖ה אֶל־אֲחוֹתָ֑הּ לְאִ֗ישׁ שְׁתַּ֤יִם מְכַסּוֹת֙ לָהֵ֔נָּה וּלְאִ֗ישׁ שְׁתַּ֤יִם מְכַסּוֹת֙ לָהֵ֔נָּה אֵ֖ת גְּוִיֹּתֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And under the vault their wings [were] straight, a woman toward her sister; to each two covering to them, and to each two covering to them, their bodies.
pieces: Under the vault their wings were stretched out straight, one toward another, and each creature also had two wings covering its body.

L.23: And under the vault their wings [were] straight, one toward the other; each had two covering them, and each had two covering them, their bodies.

R.23: Under the dome, each creature's wings were stretched out straight toward the creature next to it. Each one also had two wings that covered its body.

decisions.choice: each had two covering ... and each had two covering: a second pair covering the body
decisions.reason: The clause is said twice, perhaps for the two sides of each creature or for the creatures on each side, and the verse ends with what they covered: their bodies. It repeats verse 11: one pair of wings reached out to touch the next creature, and the other pair covered the body.

decisions.choice: a woman toward her sister: one toward another
decisions.reason: The same idiom as in verse 9, used because "wings" is feminine.

decisions.choice: each creature also had two wings covering its body (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the repeated clause once (m1). Literal keeps both.

records.source: וָאֶשְׁמַ֣ע אֶת־ק֣וֹל כַּנְפֵיהֶ֡ם כְּקוֹל֩ מַ֨יִם רַבִּ֤ים כְּקוֹל־שַׁדַּי֙ בְּלֶכְתָּ֔ם ק֥וֹל הֲמֻלָּ֖ה כְּק֣וֹל מַחֲנֶ֑ה בְּעָמְדָ֖ם תְּרַפֶּ֥ינָה כַנְפֵיהֶֽן׃
records.gloss: And I heard the sound of their wings like [the] sound of waters many, like [the] voice of Shaddai, in their going, [the] sound of tumult like [the] sound of a camp; in their standing they let drop their wings.
pieces: When they moved, I heard the sound of their wings. It was like the roar of rushing waters, like the voice of the Almighty, like the noise of an army camp. When they stood still, they lowered their wings.

L.24: And I heard the sound of their wings, like the sound of many waters, like the voice of the Almighty, when they went, a sound of tumult, like the sound of an army camp; when they stood still, they let their wings drop.

R.24: When they moved, I heard the sound of their wings. It was like the roar of a flood, like the voice of God All-Powerful, like the noise of a huge army. When they stopped, they let their wings drop.

decisions.choice: the Almighty: an ancient name of God
decisions.reason: *Shaddai* is an old name of God, used with the patriarchs (Genesis 17:1; Exodus 6:3) and often in Job. Its origin is uncertain; "Almighty" is the traditional sense. Here "the voice of the Almighty" is thunder, as in Psalm 29:3-4 and in 10:5, where the sound of the cherubim's wings is "like the voice of God Almighty when he speaks".

decisions.choice: like the sound of many waters: a sound like a great flood
decisions.reason: The roar of many waters is the sound of great power. When the glory of the LORD returns to the temple, his voice is "like the sound of many waters" (43:2). Revelation 1:15 and 14:2 take up the picture.

decisions.choice: a sound of tumult, like the sound of an army camp: the noise of a great crowd
decisions.reason: The first word is rare (Jeremiah 11:16) and means the roar of a crowd or a storm. The camp is the camp of an army, with its din of men and horses.

decisions.choice: the Almighty (L, B); God All-Powerful (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for *Shaddai* in the prophets, as in Isaiah. Readable says "a flood" for "many waters" and "a huge army" for "a camp".

records.source: וַיְהִי־ק֕וֹל מֵעַ֕ל לָרָקִ֖יעַ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־רֹאשָׁ֑ם בְּעָמְדָ֖ם תְּרַפֶּ֥ינָה כַנְפֵיהֶֽן׃
records.gloss: And there was a voice from above to the vault which [was] over their head; in their standing they let drop their wings.
pieces: Then a voice came from above the vault over their heads, as they stood still with their wings lowered.

L.25: And there was a voice from above the vault that [was] over their heads; when they stood still, they let their wings drop.

R.25: Then there was a voice from above the dome over their heads. The creatures stood still and let their wings drop.

decisions.choice: a voice: the voice of the one on the throne
decisions.reason: The same word means a sound or a voice. Here it comes from above the vault, where the throne is (verse 26), and is distinct from the sound of the wings, which has stopped. It anticipates the voice that speaks to Ezekiel in verse 28 and 2:1.

decisions.choice: when they stood still, they let their wings drop: the end of verse 24 repeated
decisions.reason: The last clause repeats the end of verse 24. Here it sets the scene for the voice: the creatures fall silent and still, and then the voice is heard.

decisions.choice: as they stood still (B); The creatures stood still (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced joins the repeated clause to the voice as a description of the moment it spoke. Readable gives it its own sentence and names the creatures.

records.source: וּמִמַּ֗עַל לָרָקִ֨יעַ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־רֹאשָׁ֔ם כְּמַרְאֵ֥ה אֶֽבֶן־סַפִּ֖יר דְּמ֣וּת כִּסֵּ֑א וְעַל֙ דְּמ֣וּת הַכִּסֵּ֔א דְּמ֞וּת כְּמַרְאֵ֥ה אָדָ֛ם עָלָ֖יו מִלְמָֽעְלָה׃
records.gloss: And from above to the vault which [was] over their head, like [the] appearance of a stone of sapphire, [the] likeness of a throne; and on the likeness of the throne a likeness like [the] appearance of a human on it from above.
pieces: Above the vault over their heads was something that looked like a throne, like sapphire in appearance. And on what looked like a throne, high above, was a figure that looked like a human being.

L.26: And above the vault that [was] over their heads [there was], like the appearance of a sapphire stone, the likeness of a throne; and on the likeness of the throne, high above, [was] a likeness like the appearance of a human being.

R.26: Above the dome over their heads was something that looked like a throne. It looked like it was made of sapphire. High above, on what looked like a throne, was a figure that looked like a human being.

decisions.choice: sapphire: a deep blue stone, most likely lapis lazuli
decisions.reason: The stone is the one under the feet of the God of Israel in Exodus 24:10. It was deep blue, the color of the sky, and was most likely lapis lazuli, a blue stone flecked with gold; the clear gem now called sapphire was little known then. The wording follows Exodus 24:10.

decisions.choice: a likeness like the appearance of a human being: God appears in human form
decisions.reason: On the throne Ezekiel sees a figure in human form. The words are chosen with great care: not "a man" but "a likeness like the appearance of a human being". The prophet does not say that God is a man or that he saw God directly (see 1:28). Daniel's vision of the Ancient of Days on a throne (Daniel 7:9) and John's vision of the one seated on the throne (Revelation 4:2-3) stand in the same line.

decisions.choice: a throne: the LORD is king
decisions.reason: Isaiah saw "the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up" in the temple (Isaiah 6:1). Ezekiel sees the same throne by a canal in Babylon, with no temple near: the LORD reigns over the exiles too.

decisions.choice: a human being, with no gender setting (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The word is the same as in verses 5, 8 and 10, but here it describes the form in which God appears, and the gender setting is never used for God. Every level says "a human being", which is what the word means. Balanced and Readable shorten "a likeness like the appearance of" to "a figure that looked like", keeping a hedge (see 1:28).

records.source: וָאֵ֣רֶא׀כְּעֵ֣ין חַשְׁמַ֗ל כְּמַרְאֵה־אֵ֤שׁ בֵּֽית־לָהּ֙ סָבִ֔יב מִמַּרְאֵ֥ה מָתְנָ֖יו וּלְמָ֑עְלָה וּמִמַּרְאֵ֤ה מָתְנָיו֙ וּלְמַ֔טָּה רָאִ֨יתִי֙ כְּמַרְאֵה־אֵ֔שׁ וְנֹ֥גַֽהּ ל֖וֹ סָבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: And I saw like [the] gleam of chashmal, like [the] appearance of fire, a house for it all around, from [the] appearance of his waist and upward; and from [the] appearance of his waist and downward I saw like [the] appearance of fire, and brightness [was] to him all around.
pieces: From what looked like {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} waist upward, I saw something like gleaming metal, like fire enclosed all around. From what looked like {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} waist downward, I saw what looked like fire, and brightness surrounded {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.27: And I saw [something] like the gleam of amber, like the appearance of fire enclosed all around, from the appearance of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hips and upward; and from the appearance of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hips and downward I saw [something] like the appearance of fire, and [there was] brightness around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.27: From what looked like {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} waist up, I saw something like shining metal, as if it were full of fire. From what looked like {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} waist down, I saw something like fire. A bright light shone all around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: like the appearance of fire, a house for it all around: fire enclosed on every side
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says literally "like the appearance of fire, a house for it all around". It seems to picture the gleaming upper body as a casing, with fire inside it on every side. The phrase is hard, and its exact picture is uncertain.

decisions.choice: amber: the same word as in verse 4
decisions.reason: The figure on the throne shines with the same brilliant substance seen at the heart of the storm in verse 4. See the note there. The description repeats "appearance" again and again, even for the figure's waist: Ezekiel describes, but keeps his distance (see 1:28).

decisions.choice: his, him: deity_pronoun spans (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The figure is "the likeness of the glory of the LORD" (verse 28), so the pronouns for it take the setting for pronouns for God, though the description keeps its hedges. *Chashmal* is "amber", "gleaming metal" or "shining metal" as in verse 4.

decisions.choice: From what looked like his waist upward (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the part of the figure first, so that the reader knows what is being described, and keep the hedge "what looked like" (see 1:28). Readable says "as if it were full of fire" for the hard phrase in m1.

records.source: כְּמַרְאֵ֣ה הַקֶּ֡שֶׁת אֲשֶׁר֩ יִֽהְיֶ֨ה בֶעָנָ֜ן בְּי֣וֹם הַגֶּ֗שֶׁם כֵּ֣ן מַרְאֵ֤ה הַנֹּ֨גַהּ֙ סָבִ֔יב ה֕וּא מַרְאֵ֖ה דְּמ֣וּת כְּבוֹד־יְהוָ֑ה וָֽאֶרְאֶה֙ וָאֶפֹּ֣ל עַל־פָּנַ֔י וָאֶשְׁמַ֖ע ק֥וֹל מְדַבֵּֽר׃ס
records.gloss: Like [the] appearance of the bow which is in the cloud on [the] day of rain, so [was the] appearance of the brightness all around; it [was the] appearance of [the] likeness of [the] glory of Yahweh. And I saw, and I fell on my face, and I heard [the] voice of [one] speaking.
pieces: Like a rainbow in the clouds on a day of rain, so was the brightness on every side. This was what the likeness of the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} looked like. When I saw it, I fell face down, and I heard the voice of someone speaking.

L.28: Like the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud on a day of rain, so [was] the appearance of the surrounding brightness. Such [was] the appearance of the likeness of the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I saw [it], and I fell on my face, and I heard the voice of one speaking.

R.28: The bright light all around looked like a rainbow in the clouds on a rainy day. This was something that looked like the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. When I saw it, I bowed down with my face to the ground. Then I heard someone speaking.

decisions.choice: the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD: Ezekiel will not say that he saw God directly
decisions.reason: Throughout the vision Ezekiel uses "likeness" and "appearance": "the likeness of four living creatures" (verse 5), "the likeness of a throne", "a likeness like the appearance of a human being" (verse 26), and now, at the end, "the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD". The hedges are deliberate. He describes what he saw by comparing it with fire, metal, gems and the rainbow, and every comparison holds him back from saying that he saw the LORD himself, whom no one can see and live (Exodus 33:20). Even the glory is seen only in its likeness. The same care governs the visions of chapters 8 and 10 and 43:2-5.

decisions.choice: the glory of the LORD: the visible splendor of the LORD's presence
decisions.reason: The word for glory means weight, and so honor and splendor. "The glory of the LORD" is the LORD's presence made visible, as in the cloud and fire on Sinai (Exodus 24:16-17) and the cloud that filled the tabernacle and the temple (Exodus 40:34-35; 1 Kings 8:10-11). In Ezekiel the glory appears to the exiles here and in 3:23, leaves the temple before Jerusalem falls (10:18-19; 11:22-23) and returns to the new temple at the end (43:2-5).

decisions.choice: the bow in the cloud on a day of rain: the rainbow
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the bow set in the clouds after the flood as the sign of God's covenant (Genesis 9:13-16). Revelation 4:3 sees a rainbow around the throne of God.

decisions.choice: I heard the voice of one speaking: the speech begins in 2:1
decisions.reason: The chapter ends as the voice begins to speak; its words follow in 2:1. Ezekiel falls on his face in awe, as others do before the LORD's glory (Leviticus 9:24; 3:23; 43:3).

decisions.choice: the appearance of the likeness of (L); what the likeness of ... looked like (B); something that looked like (R)
decisions.reason: Ezekiel's hedges are kept at every level (m1). Literal keeps the whole phrase "the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD", because this is where the chapter's hedges come to rest; Balanced says "what the likeness of ... looked like", which keeps both hedges. Readable shortens it to "something that looked like", which keeps a hedge, as the table for Ezekiel allows.

decisions.choice: I fell face down (B); I bowed down with my face to the ground (R)
decisions.reason: To fall on one's face is to throw oneself to the ground in awe or worship. Balanced and Readable say it in current English. Readable says "a rainy day" and "someone speaking".
